replacement.title: Receive the loose goalie outlet
replacement.objective: Prepare for a goalie outlet while treating the puck as loose until a player controls it.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net. The Navy goalie has released an outlet, but the puck is still loose near YOU. Gold 1 is nearby on the same side. D2 is across the net and C is nearer the middle. The freeze does not establish the puck’s travel direction or a clean reception.
cues: The goalie has released an outlet.
The puck is loose near YOU.
Gold 1 is nearby on the same side.

questions.prompt: Who controls the outlet puck at the freeze?
questions.explanation: The puck is shown loose in transit, so no player has possession at the freeze.

questions.prompt: Which two receiver checks belong before the touch?

options.text: D2 or C as a support option
The release label confirms a clean reception

questions.explanation: Pressure and support shape the first touch; the goalie release does not decide its result.

questions.prompt: Arrange a loose-outlet routine.

options.text: Choose the touch from the updated lane

questions.explanation: Finding the puck and checking pressure can overlap with approaching using a support option; both can happen while skating. The touch still comes last because it must match whichever lane is actually open once YOU get there.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare an approach to the loose puck.
questions.explanation: The example is closer to the puck, but also closer to Gold 1. Check the next touch and the routes toward D2 or C; arriving near the puck does not establish control.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 reaches the planned touch lane first. What should be reconsidered?

options.text: Recheck access; protect only after control, or find reachable support
Assume the goalie can retrieve it again

questions.explanation: If Gold 1 reaches the lane first, reassess whether YOU can recover the loose puck. Protection or a pass requires a playable touch; neither is already established.

questions.prompt: What could YOU communicate before the goalie releases another outlet?
questions.explanation: Name the pressure side and the support YOU can see. A short call can help the release choose a reachable lane, then update after the puck is touched.

replacement.title: Read the second option in a two-on-one
replacement.objective: Update a two-on-one choice when a defender changes the passing connection.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net. YOU control the puck and F2 is the second attacker. Gold 1 occupies the direct line between YOU and F2. The goalie is near the net; no save or finish is established.
cues: F2 is the second Navy attacker.
Gold 1 occupies the direct pass lane.

questions.prompt: What has Gold 1 changed?
questions.explanation: Gold 1 is stated to have moved into the direct passing connection.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should shape the next touch?

options.text: The two-on-one label decides the finish

questions.explanation: The defender, goalie and support route determine whether a shot, pass or protection is useful.

questions.prompt: Arrange a changed two-on-one read.

options.text: Compare the carrier and second option

questions.explanation: Locating Gold 1 and F2 can overlap with comparing the carrier and second option; both are part of the same scan. Re-checking the goalie and lane still comes last because the read must reflect whichever option is open right before the touch.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different angle toward F2 and the net.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier’s passing and shooting angles. Recheck Gold 1, F2 and the goalie before choosing; the new point does not establish an open lane.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 turns toward YOU and F2 gains separation. What could improve?

options.text: A pass if F2 remains reachable, or a shot if the goalie gives room
Ignore F2 and shoot through the defender

questions.explanation: F2 separation changes the branch, while the goalie and defender still determine whether the pass or shot is usable.

questions.prompt: How can feedback respect both a possible shot and a possible pass?
questions.explanation: Tie the choice to Gold 1, F2 and the goalie. If the defender closes the carrier but F2 is reachable, pass; if F2 is covered and the carrier lane remains open, consider the shot.

replacement.objective: Arrive as second support for a loose touch while leaving the first player room to compete.

questions.prompt: Which Navy player has the first wall-contest role?
questions.explanation: F1 is the named first contest player; YOU are the second support.

questions.prompt: Which two cues make second support useful?

options.text: The next loose touch from the contest

questions.explanation: Read the next loose touch and whether C can be reached without crowding F1. Gold 2 is already close to C, so that outlet is not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Arrange a second-support read.

options.text: Track the loose touch and C
Choose recovery or support after the touch

questions.explanation: Staying outside F1's space and tracking the loose touch and C happen together, not one after the other. The final step, choosing recovery or support, only becomes clear once the touch actually resolves.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare support outside F1’s contest.
questions.explanation: The example is farther from the wall contest and closer to C. Compare that inside support with the chance to recover the next loose touch; Gold 2 is near C and the route is not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 closes C as the puck rolls free. What should be checked?

options.text: The carrier side, another outlet and the inside lane

questions.explanation: C is no longer the same outlet, so update the support and recovery choices.

questions.prompt: What is a useful second-player job when F1 does not win the puck cleanly?
questions.explanation: Track the loose touch and the inside threat while leaving F1 room. After a playable touch, compare C with another reachable outlet. No one controls the puck yet.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is unavailable during this rep?

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter with one support option missing?

options.text: The change requires a dump regardless of pressure

questions.explanation: A reset and a forward route preserve choices while the line change reduces one support option.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possession read during the change.

options.text: Locate pressure and the remaining support
Protect or move to the reachable connection

questions.explanation: Keep scanning pressure and support while protecting or moving the puck. Recheck throughout the change, including when the replacement arrives; this is one suggested order, not a reason to stop scanning.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a reset toward D2 with a forward route toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example is closer to D2 and farther from F1. Compare pressure and both routes before using either; shorter distance does not guarantee an open pass.

questions.prompt: A new F3 appears in a clear middle lane. What can YOU reconsider?

options.text: A middle connection if pressure and support make it reachable
Leave the puck without checking the new lane
Assume the change makes every route safe

questions.explanation: The new player changes the support picture, but the carrier still checks access and pressure.

questions.prompt: Why does a line change call for a possession read rather than one fixed action?
questions.explanation: The available outlet set changes while the puck and pressure remain live. Name D2, the forward route and the arriving F3, then choose the connection that stays reachable.

replacement.objective: Keep a possession route available when the slot is shaded and a low teammate can become the next outlet.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. YOU control near the puck-side half wall; Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot, F1 is behind the goal line, and D1 holds the high point with Gold 3 nearby. The rep asks YOU to compare a connected reset with the crowded inside option.

Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot.
F1 is a low outlet and D1 holds the point.

sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

questions.prompt: Which Navy teammate is positioned behind Gold’s goal line?
questions.explanation: F1 is behind Gold’s goal line as a possible low outlet. Check the defenders before assuming a pass can reach F1.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a reset?

options.text: Whether the low route to F1 is reachable
The half-wall label decides the next pass

questions.explanation: The defender and low outlet determine whether the reset can preserve possession.

questions.prompt: Arrange a connected reset.

options.text: Locate F2, F1 and the high point
Protect the puck from the slot shade
Use the reachable outlet and scan again

questions.explanation: Scan F2, F1 and D1 while protecting the puck, then use a reachable option and scan again. Scanning and protection can overlap; a named outlet is not necessarily open.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare the routes toward F1, F2 and D1.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier angle and brings YOU closer to all three teammates, but also closer to Gold 1 and Gold 3. Recheck the defenders before using any route.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves F2 to pressure YOU on the wall. What should be weighed?

options.text: A quick F2 connection if the slot remains reachable, or F1 support
Force F2 because the defender moved
Send the puck low without checking F1

questions.explanation: The defender move may open F2, but carrier angle and F1 support still determine the connected choice.

questions.prompt: Name two support areas in this reset and explain their different value.
questions.explanation: F1 offers a low outlet, while F2 offers an inside option if Gold 1 leaves it reachable. D1 is a high reset to check too, with Gold 3 nearby. Naming an outlet does not guarantee it is open.
